title: Shadow cache & kernel decomposition — weekly sync
content:
Week: 2028-W40
Date: 2028-10-04
Attendees: Amina Patel (owner), Jonah Kim, Luis Ortega, Priya Shah, Maya Chen, Ricardo Alvarez
Meeting length: 45m
Location: Zoom + #serving-runtime
Objective: Weekly consolidation of kernel decomposition progress, shadow KV cache behavior, and next-step batching experiments. Focus this week was triage of a tail-latency anomaly observed during a small DDoS-like traffic pattern, plus validating the initial kernel-split perf gains.

1) Quick summary
- Kernel decomposition PRs 1987 and 1994 landed in branch "kernel-decomp/stage-1" for smoke tests (Jonah).
- Shadow KV cache saw a +17% write amplification in high-prefix churn workloads; root cause narrowed to eviction ordering bug in shadow-layer (Luis).
- Microbatching experiment #prefill-42 reduced p50 token latency by 8% on short-context 128-token requests, but p95 regressed under bursty patterns.
- Decision: keep shadow-cache enabled for internal canary but gate its writes under a sliding window heuristic until eviction fix is in prod.

2) Incident note (tail-latency spike)
What happened: During a synthetic burst from load-testing harness, p95 token latency jumped from 72ms to 320ms on one node group for ~6 minutes.
Initial hypotheses: kernel scheduling starvation vs. KV eviction thrashing vs. hardware thermal throttle.
Findings:
- CPU/GPU thermal and utilization metrics were normal.
- Trace logs show a burst of large prefix misses that caused synchronous cache-population on the serving thread (shadow cache attempted to warm KV entries synchronously when miss_count > threshold).
- Eviction order used LRU across multi-shard shadow arrays which caused hot-prefixes to be evicted and re-populated repeatedly under churn.
Action taken:
- Rolled back synchronous warm path; enabled async backfill (toggle: SHADOW_CACHE_SYNC_WARM=false) at 2028-10-04T14:12 UTC.
- Disabled shadow-cache writes to canary traffic for 30m to stop the thrash.
Follow-up tickets: JIRA-INF-3421 (eviction ordering fix), JIRA-INF-3478 (add chaos test for backfill path).

3) Kernel decomposition status
- What landed: PR 1987 (split scheduler loop into light-weight worker pool + IO poller). PR 1994 (isolate attention kernel dispatcher to a separate runtime shim).
- Early perf numbers (internal lab, A100 cluster, seq=128): baseline v1.8 -> kernel-decomp/stage-1
  - p50 token latency: 72ms -> 66ms
  - p95 token latency: 220ms -> 198ms
  - throughput (tokens/s): 18,400 -> 19,300
- Notes: Gains are consistent for short sequences but vary for long-context flows due to new dispatcher heuristics.
- Outstanding: need to reconcile scheduler affinity for mixed CPU/GPU workloads (ticket: INF-3552 assigned to Priya).

4) Batching experiments
- Experiment A (microbatch/prefill-42): group size dynamic up to 8, prefill allowed for requests with same model+route within 10ms window. Results on canary:
  - Short-context (<=128 tokens): p50 -8%, cost/token -4%
  - Bursty mixed workload: p95 +24%
- Experiment B (adaptive-delay-heuristic): add 3ms delay when queue depth < 4 to improve coalescing. Results:
  - Improved p95 slightly in bursty mixed by 6% but increased median by 1.5%
- Decision: keep microbatching as opt-in for routes where latency SLO allows slight p95 regression; continue tuning adaptive-delay parameters. Jira ticket INF-3499 to parameterize per-route heuristics.

5) Shadow KV cache plan and actions
- Problem: write amplification + eviction thrash under churn.
- Short-term mitigations completed:
  1) Toggle off synchronous warm path (done).
  2) Limit shadow-cache write QPS per node (config: SHADOW_WRITE_QPS_LIMIT=2000) — applied to canary (Maya).
  3) Add metric: shadow_eviction_repop_rate (Luis) — now emitted to Prometheus; dashboard created.
- Medium-term fixes:
  - Implement FIFO within hot-partition to protect hot prefixes (spike protection) — owner: Ricardo, ETA: 2028-10-11.
  - Rewrite eviction comparator to use weighted recency + access frequency (ticket JIRA-INF-3421) — owner: Luis, ETA: 2028-10-18.
  - Add a lightweight probabilistic bloom filter to reduce unnecessary backfills for cold keys — proposal under review (Amina).
- Long-term: evaluate moving shadow-cache to separate lightweight process with an async replication stream to serving nodes (design doc due Q1 2029).

6) Open action items (owners + due dates)
- Jonah: complete load-test harness scenario that reproduces LRU-thrash (due 2028-10-07).
- Luis: land eviction comparator patch + unit tests (JIRA-INF-3421) (due 2028-10-11).
- Priya: bench scheduler affinity changes on mixed CPU/GPU infra (INF-3552) (due 2028-10-12).
- Maya: monitor shadow_eviction_repop_rate dashboard and report anomalies after config change (due 2028-10-06).
- Ricardo: prototype FIFO hot-partition shield (due 2028-10-11).
- Amina: write short design note for async shadow-cache process (due 2028-10-18).

7) Notes to reviewers / decisions to surface to Product
- Product & Console: we should expose a temporary flag in Console to disable shadow-cache writes per-deployment (privacy/ops safety). This is low-friction for SREs to mitigate production thrash quickly. (Product owner: Maya to coordinate).
- UX: Add a visible metric card for "shadow cache repop rate" and an alert when >1000/min sustained for 5m.

8) Risks and mitigation
- Risk: rolling out kernel-decomp without scheduler affinity tuning could degrade long-context throughput for some customers. Mitigation: gate stage-1 on canary and provide a rollback path (rollback token named kernel-decomp-rollback-1).
- Risk: shadow-cache async backfill may introduce temporary memory pressure on the backfill worker. Mitigation: limit backfill concurrency and add backpressure signal to RPCs.

9) Quick logs / debug checklist (for oncall)
- How to reproduce the thrash locally: run load-harness scenario "prefix-churn-rapid" with --clients=120 --rate=3000 --seq=128.
- Toggle to disable sync warm: export SHADOW_CACHE_SYNC_WARM=false && restart canary service.
- Check metric: shadow_eviction_repop_rate on Grafana (dashboard: infra/serving/shadow-cache).
- If p95 remains high after rolling toggles, capture a kernel dispatcher flame with perf and upload to the incident ticket.

10) Misc notes and brainstorms (freeform)
- Consider a small LRU-style aging window that demotes keys slower than current immediate LRU. Might flatten repop spikes without adding heavy metadata.
- Could use a tiny per-prefix token-bucket to throttle repopulations; cheap to implement and may buy time while eviction algorithm is improved.
- Worth experimenting with a hybrid async-early-warm: spawn backfill async but start a micro-prefill of first N KV bytes inline to reduce first-token latency.

Next sync: 2028-10-11, 11:00 PT. Please add any follow-ups in the linked Jira tickets and tag @eng-serving-runtime in PR comments for fast triage.

End of note.
